info.title: Agentic Finance Graph — public state API
info.description: The machine-readable tape of the AI-agent economy. Free, unauthenticated, CC BY 4.0 with attribution to https://agenticfinancegraph.com. Live values are read from public APIs and on-chain eth_call; cited values are imported research and are labeled kind=cited. Registration counts are never a live-agent count. Paid evidence packs (/check/{kind}) are sold per call over x402 v2 on Base in USDC: a bare GET answers 402 with the requirements; retry with a signed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. Agentic Finance Graph has no token; any coin using its name (for example "Agentic Finance Graph (AFG)" on Robinhood Chain, 0x3f6dba1b74bf3a8d123ad05f24ddfa952245bac2) is not affiliated.
info.x-guidance: Free routes (/api/*) need no key and no payment; read /api/state first for every current figure with its definition id and as_of. Paid evidence packs: GET /check/{kind}?id=<ERC-8004 token id on Base> answers 402 with x402 v2 requirements (USDC on Base, exact scheme, amount in atomic units, payTo); sign the payment and retry with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header; the 200 body is the pack with its receipt. Kinds and prices in USDC: liveness 0.01, paygraph 0.05, drain 0.02, incidents 0.01, peer 0.01, bundle 0.10, reval 0.25; the 402 states the exact amount before anything is charged. MCP clients can read the same free data at https://agenticfinancegraph.com/mcp. Every figure is a measurement with a time, never an estimate; quote the counted total only beside the top-wallet share and the median.

get.summary: Historical archive of the tape at two resolutions
get.description: Two-resolution history. daily[] keeps one point per UTC day for two years and is never evicted by live traffic; recent[] keeps 5-minute points for 48 hours. The response stitches them for the requested window. Points marked source=defillama-historical are daily backfill, source=live are our own snapshots, source=live-close is the last snapshot of a completed day. A gap means nobody visited during that bucket — gaps are visible in coverage rather than interpolated away.

get.summary: Third-party agent catalogs joined to our own qualifier
get.description:
Marketplaces and registries each publish a census of themselves; none of those counts answer whether the listed names are economic actors. This endpoint runs our qualifier over their catalogs and reports the result against OUR denominator.

Read three things before quoting any figure here.

1. `attempted` is the identities WE ingested and checked — never the partner's own published census. A rate over somebody else's marketing total cannot be reproduced.
2. `moved_usdc` is NOT L7. It means the declared wallet sent USDC to a different address after the identity existed. From a raw wallet read a token launch, a bonding-curve buy and a DEX swap are indistinguishable from a payment for work, so L7 is withheld on catalogs where we cannot yet see job state, and the blocker is named in the response.
3. Each partner block carries a `caveats` array. The caveats are part of the number.

A measured zero and a withheld value are different things and are represented differently: 0 is a finding, `null` means we have not earned the figure yet. Worked examples are desk-only and are stripped from anonymous responses, with the count of what was withheld reported rather than silently omitted. Cached 5 minutes at the edge.

evidence_withheld.description: Worked examples removed from this response.

partners.description: One block per partner: fetch, virtuals, olas, x402, wallets_7702, circle, bankr.

attempted.description: Identities we ingested and ran the qualifier on. The denominator for every rate in this block.

distinct_wallets.description: Distinct addresses behind those declarations. Lower than declared_a_wallet wherever operators reuse one wallet across many identities.

on_shared_wallet.description: Identities declaring a wallet another identity in the same catalog also declares. Excluded from `bound`.

bound.description: Identities bound to a sole-declarant wallet.

qualified.description: Bound wallets we have actually read on-chain.

moved_usdc.description: Qualified wallets that sent USDC to a different address after the identity existed. NOT L7.

had_history_before_launch.description: Wallets whose USDC history predates their identity. That history is excluded from every figure here.

blocker.description: Present when a whole partner block is empty because we have measured nothing.

post.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, prompts/list, prompts/get, resources/list, resources/read. Twenty-six read-only tools: market_state, find_agent, agent_record, ranked_agents, detections, definition, metric_history, list_metrics, since_last, counterparty_preview, agent_statement, pay_check, payer_set, agent_stability, agent_independence, ladder_dynamics, verify_sum_log, self_check, agent_pattern, payee_facts, gate_check, agent_pass, blast_radius, canary_register, canary_status, evidence_pack_quote; five prompts (start_here, daily_brief, check_before_paying, explain_agent, where_agents_pay). Free; no session and no key. Server version 1.9.1 (7 Nov 2026). Tool calls count against the same per-address limits as the plain routes, and against 120 tool calls a minute in all; over a limit the answer is an error that names the limit, and nothing is run.

get.description: One address on Base: its label with category, basis and evidence link, contract or plain key (and any EIP-7702 delegation), registered agents that paid it in 30 days and all time with counted USD, whether it is a registered agent's bound wallet, an x402 seller or an address our poisoning watch saw planted as a look-alike, and its USDC, USDT and EURC transfers over the last 48 hours, read live (capped at 2,000 per direction and marked when capped). An address with no label and no record in our tables is a 404 before any payment.

Each step is explained by a dated entry in /api/changepoints, by a checked note (a move of the world, measured two ways), marked settling (the series is under a week old), or left open; the data check unexplained_step warns on open steps from the last 14 days.

post.description: Send an A2A JSON-RPC request with method message/send. Text is routed by what it asks (an agent id or 0x address, a check before paying, detections, the top of the rank, the market state); a data part {"tool": "<MCP tool name>", "arguments": {...}} calls a tool of the MCP server directly. Every reply is a Message (no tasks, no streaming). The agent card is at /.well-known/agent-card.json. Tool calls count against the same per-address limits as the plain routes, and against 120 tool calls a minute in all; over a limit the answer is an error that names the limit, and nothing is run.

Nothing per visitor is kept: no address, no user agent, no query string, no body. Cloudflare answers some requests from its cache and those never reach the origin, so every figure is a floor; our own checks are included. Definition usage.origin.v1. post.summary: The Gate: check one payment against a policy before it is made
post.description: One call before an agent pays. Returns block, warn, log or allow with every reason, the nine payee facts, the Watch reading of this payment against the agent's own history, and a signed receipt (gate.receipt.v2: the policy by name and by the SHA-256 of all its limits). Advisory: the caller decides, nothing is blocked by us. A payment on which nothing fired answers allow with no reasons. The default policy is log-only; named policies are at /api/gate/policies, or send your own in the AP2 constraint vocabulary. An unknown constraint fails closed. Free tier: 30 calls a minute per address. A Bearer Desk session makes the check identified: its receipt goes into the signed log. Browsers may call it from any origin.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bearer <Desk session>. Optional.

agent.description: The paying agent: token id, act_8453_N, slug or bound wallet.

policy.description: Your own policy: allowed_payees, amount_range, budget, agent_recurrence, execution_date, new_payee, refuse_conditions, signal.

client_ref.description: Optional. A random string your client keeps and sends with every check. Checks with the same client_ref count against each other for 12 hours, until the ledger holds the payments (gate.context.v2), so a payment split into small parts meets the same limits. Keep it outside the reach of the model you guard.

400.description: the body is not {agent, payee, amount_usd, policy_name | policy}

404.description: the agent is not a Base ERC-8004 registration we know

422.description: the agent has more than 20,000 counted payments; its history is not scored at request time

429.description: 30 Gate calls a minute per address on the free tier; nothing was recorded

503.description: the check could not run; nothing is recorded and nothing is substituted. Your client's fail mode decides. Also the answer when checks of one agent under one client_ref or Desk session, which are decided one at a time, leave a check waiting longer than 5 seconds for its turn.

get.summary: Agent Books: one agent's month as a signed statement
get.description: What one registration paid and received on Base in a closed month or to date: counted payments, what left its control, what was left out and why, receipts, detections, transfers of the registration. Signed, written into our signed log, and committed to by a daily Base transaction, so the receiver can check it without trusting us (agent.books.v1; verifier: afg booksverify). A record of observed facts: not an audit, an opinion, or a statement about tax. Without parameters: what it is. Every signed answer carries permalink (/api/books?id=<books_id>), which returns that same statement later; a request by agent and period on a later day makes a new statement for that day.
